scenes.headline: How a splat scene becomes a bundle of WebP images
scenes.sub: SOG: Spatially Ordered Gaussians, an open splat format
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Wicket! A Gaussian splat scene is huge. Here is how SOG shrinks it into a handful of WebP images.

scenes.text: SOG stores each splat field as a quantized, spatially-ordered WebP image instead of a float dump, so the whole scene compresses like a picture.
scenes.say: The idea: store each splat field as a quantized WebP image, and order the splats in space, so the scene compresses like a picture.

steps.say: A splat is a position, a rotation, a scale, and a spherical-harmonic colour.
Quantize the position to sixteen bits an axis. It splits across two WebP images.
Keep the rotation's smallest three numbers and drop the fourth. One more image.
Swap the big colour vector for a single index into a shared palette.
Zip the images with a tiny meta file, and that is the SOG bundle.

scenes.title: Bytes per splat
scenes.say: The same splat costs two hundred forty-eight bytes in the float file, and thirteen point six four in SOG. Eighteen times smaller.

left.title: means_l, low bits
left.say: The low position bits are noise. Neighbours differ randomly, so WebP keeps almost all of it.

right.title: means_u, high bits
right.say: The high bits barely change between splats that sit together. In Morton order, WebP erases most of them.

steps.say: Here is that sixty-five megabyte file, drawn live in the open viewer.
The floating cages are the cameras the scene was built from.

scenes.text: Quantization does most of the shrink. The spatial order makes the high position bits almost free.

recap: Each field becomes a WebP image
scenes.say: To recap: every splat field becomes a quantized WebP image, ordered in space so WebP compresses neighbours.
